html_value.text: After our first steps in the introduction to mathematics (; ; ; ), this volume continues exploring fundamental operations and different cultures. We will broaden our knowledge by looking, in greater detail, at everything around us: from the smallest things, such as atoms, to the cultures and civilizations that have existed — and still exist — and that gave us the world we know today.

Menu

    1. First Steps: Return to the main menu of the First Steps section.

    2. Volume 1 – The foundations of the universe: In this volume, we study — through different cultures — how the numbers we use every day were discovered, and we explore how they are used at the different stages of our lives.

value.name: Continuity
value.desc: We rarely see gaps around us: things seem to connect. In this text, we learn to connect them by drawing rectangles over a line of numbers to fill the spaces in between.

value.name: Limiting
value.desc: By dividing one large rectangle into ten smaller equal ones, we limit their size — and, by limiting sizes, we learn to measure the values between the integers.

value.name: Greater or Smaller? (Real Numbers)
value.desc: A game that asks which of two numbers is greater: from single-digit integers to millions with one decimal place, in four levels.

value.name: Naming
value.desc: Numbers have names too: units, tens, hundreds... After seeing how we can fill in the values between numbers, how about giving them their proper names?

value.name: Sequence games (Decimal order)
value.desc: A game to connect each number with the name of its family, from quintillions to trillionths, in three levels.

value.name: Reality
value.desc: Once we can place decimal numbers between the integers, we stop merely counting and start describing reality itself — and we meet the families of numbers, starting with the natural numbers.

value.name: Cooking with numbers
value.desc: Recipes are written with natural numbers — cups, spoons, minutes — yet the dish that comes out of the oven is entirely real. In this text, we cook with numbers.

html_value.text: Chapter 2: Mirror, mirror on the wall...

value.name: Integers
value.desc: We have not studied all the integers yet: in this text, we meet the ones that live on the other side of the mirror, using reflections in mirrors and on the surface of water.

value.name: Same, but different
value.desc: A mirror shows the same numbers on both sides — only the sign changes. In this text, we begin calculating with numbers of opposite signs and discover that subtraction is a kind of addition.

value.name: Modulating (Part I)
value.desc: In this text, we learn that walking in the opposite direction shares many rules with walking in the direction we are used to, and we try operations on the other side of zero with the help of Copán and the Peabirú path.

value.name: Practicing addition (negative numbers)
value.desc: An application that generates random sums of negative numbers and describes each step of the calculation, so you can practice until adding negatives feels natural.

value.name: Modulating (Part II)
value.desc: In this text, we present the 'negative multiplication table' — multiplying by -1 — and how it helps us understand the other side of the number line.

value.name: Modulating (Part III)
value.desc: Continuing from the previous text, we use the 'negative multiplication table' to deepen our understanding of inclinations: paths that go up and down, like the Peabirú.

value.name: Drawing the multiplication
value.desc: In this text, we learn the recipe for drawing any multiplication table: write a formula, plot its points, and connect them.

value.name: Understanding the Multiplication Table (0 and 1)
value.desc: The multiplication table is often presented as something to memorize — but why should we ignore the knowledge that comes with it? In this text, we discover what multiplying by 0 and by 1 really means.

value.name: Understanding the Multiplication Table (2 and 3)
value.desc: In this text, we explore the relationship between multiplication and triangles while studying the tables of 2 and 3.

value.name: Understanding the Multiplication Table (4 and 5)
value.desc: In this text, we examine the relationship between triangles and mountains while studying the tables of 4 and 5.

value.name: Learning from nature
value.desc: In this text, we explore how knowledge of multiplication could have helped ancient civilizations — from the smallest house to the great works of Caral.

value.name: Understanding the Multiplication Table (6 and 7)
value.desc: In this text, we explore how the peoples of Mesopotamia used these two tables, the foundation of the way we measure time today: sixty seconds in every minute.

value.name: Understanding the Multiplication Table (8 and 9)
value.desc: What would happen if we stepped off the plane of the page? And if we went deeper, inside the shapes themselves?

value.name: Understanding the Multiplication Tables (Summary)
value.desc: After studying the 10 multiplication tables, we review the content — this time in the opposite direction, starting from the charts and working back to the general formula.

value.name: Multiplying the Findings with Groups
value.desc: A game to practice the multiplication tables: each table appears as groups of identical figures, and every correct answer reveals an archaeological finding.

value.name: Practicing multiplication by one-digit numbers
value.desc: An application that teaches multiplication by one-digit numbers in three levels, describing each step of the calculation.

value.name: Multiplying the Findings
value.desc: A game to practice the multiplication tables: every correct answer reveals an archaeological finding.

value.name: Ages and Pyramids
value.desc: What does a pyramid have in common with the dates of our birthdays? In this text, we answer with our first mathematical model.

Volume 3

  1. Volume 3 – Shapes: In this volume, we explore geometric shapes across different cultures and their applications in everyday life.
